articles.title: Japanese PM Takaichi says Russia, Japan will keep talking as ties remain chilled
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi said on Thursday (November 19, 2026) that she and Russian President Vladimir Putin held talks and agreed to keep communicating in the first such encounter between the two countries' leaders in seven years.

Speaking to reporters on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit, she said she raised the issue of Moscow's treatment of Japanese businesses in Russia and urged Putin to release a Japanese journalist detained for alleged spying during their meeting late Wednesday (November 18, 2026) in Shenzhen, China.
“We reached an agreement to maintain communication at various levels, including direct contact between the president and myself,” Ms. Takaichi said.
Japan's ties with Russia have long been strained by a territorial dispute dating back decades.

Japan lodged a protest with Russia in October over the arrest of a Japanese journalist working for the Hokkaido Shimbun newspaper on suspicion of spying, demanding that Moscow provide an explanation, consular access and humane treatment.

Moscow recently seized control of some local subsidiaries of Japan Tobacco, the largest cigarette maker in Russia, and the company reported it expects a 724 billion yen ($4.5 billion) loss for this year due to the takeover.

Earlier, Japan Tobacco had forecast a 662 billion yen profit for the financial year ending December 31. The company said it has not given up legal ownership of the Russia-based subsidiaries or withdrawn from operating in Russia.

Tensions rose in August after Mr. Putin visited Iturup, one of four Russian-controlled islands off Japan's northern coast that Tokyo also claims. Earlier this month, Tokyo protested after two Russian aircraft briefly violated Japanese airspace off southwestern Japan.

The last bilateral in-person talks between Japanese and Russian leaders were held between then-Prime Minister Shinzo Abe and Mr. Putin in September 2019, during the Eastern Economic Forum in the Russian city of Vladivostok.

Mr. Putin is attending the annual APEC summit for the first time in nine years. He, Chinese President Xi Jinping and U.S. President Donald Trump held a summit meeting on Thursday (November 19, 2026) after the APEC gathering, an event that seems to underscore Japan's diminished role as a global power.
Ms. Takaichi herself was given a very minimal reception on her arrival in Shenzhen, provoking speculation over a deliberate snub by her hosts.
When asked, Ms. Takaichi said she did not believe the summit between Mr. Xi, Mr. Trump and Mr. Putin would undermine Japan's interests.

articles.title: Riyadh's tallest building damaged as Saudi reports new Houthi attacks
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: A skyscraper in Riyadh housing the headquarters of Saudi Arabia's sovereign wealth fund was damaged on Thursday (November 19, 2026), witnesses told AFP , as the kingdom reported new attacks by Yemen's Houthis.
Saudi Arabia has been battling a surge in attacks since fighting reignited in neighbouring Yemen's civil war, where Riyadh backs the internationally recognised government against the Houthis.
In the early hours of Thursday (November 19, 2026), AFP journalists in the Saudi capital reported a powerful blast was heard.
Around the same time, civil defence authorities issued a warning for "potential danger" but said minutes later that the danger had passed.
The Saudi-led military coalition fighting the Houthis said it had "addressed a missile threat launched by the terrorist Houthi militia towards Riyadh".
"Initial assessment indicates the impact of debris, with material damage currently being surveyed," said coalition spokesman Turki al-Malki.
Witnesses later told AFP that Riyadh's Public Investment Fund Tower, which at 80 storeys is the tallest in the city, had been damaged.
"The facade is damaged across several floors, with windows blown out," said one person who requested anonymity.
"The damage also affected some of the buildings surrounding PIF tower, causing the glass facades on some to shatter. Some of the buildings are residential," the witness added.
Two other witnesses confirmed the damage to the tower, which AFP was unable to visit.
Since early September, most employees in the building had been working remotely, they told AFP .
Standing 385 metres high, the PIF tower dominates Riyadh's King Abdullah Financial District, which acts as a showcase for Saudi Arabia's economic ambitions.

articles.title: Rohingya a ‘distinct lineage’ close to Bangladeshis and Burmese: Study
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: The Rohingya are a distinct genetic group with genomic ancestry closer to Bangladeshis but considerable genetic mixture from the Burmese lineage. While this isn’t surprising from a linguistic-cultural perspective, it is the first such comprehensive study from a genomic analysis perspective.

“Burmese” here is a stand-in for East and Southeast Asian ancestry in general. The study underlines what is now a basic principle of human population genetics that all ethnic populations are a result of intermingling of multiple population groups through history.

The analysis comes on the heels of a Thursday (November 19) verdict by the International Court of Justice. In a 9-6 ruling, the court held that Myanmar had committed genocide against the Muslim minority Rohingya in the north Rakhine State. This was the verdict on a 2019 case brought to the court by The Gambia in which it accused the Myanmar government of trying to destroy the Rohingya.
The Burmese state has tried to portray the Rohingya as “outsiders” from Bangladesh to justify atrocities against them.

The genetics study, which appeared on November 17 in the peer-reviewed journal Scientific Reports , does not say anything about citizenship, but notes: “This study addresses a critical void in the evolutionary history of a deeply marginalised group and unequivocally reinforces that modern human populations are intricate mosaics of diverse ancestral lineages, fundamentally shaped by historical migrations and gene flow that transcend contemporary political boundaries.”

The main authors of the study are affiliated with a range of institutions including the Banaras Hindu University (BHU), Varanasi; BRIC-Centre for DNA Fingerprinting and Diagnostics (CDFD), Hyderabad; the University of Dhaka, Bangladesh; University of Calcutta; and Amity University, Uttar Pradesh.

“Our analyses reveal a complex genomic architecture that closely mirrors their linguistic affiliations. The Rohingya exhibit a foundational genetic affinity with eastern South Asian Indo-European speaking populations, predominantly aligning with present-day Bangladeshi communities,” the authors report.

The Rohingya migrated into the Arakan region within the last millennium and, following this, the ancestral Rohingya mixed with those with Southeast Asian ancestry from local Myanmar-related populations, they underline.

For their analysis, the researchers took blood samples from 25 Rohingya volunteers at the Cox’s Bazar refugee camp in Bangladesh, with informed consent and ethics approval from the University of Dhaka. For comparison they sampled 45 neighbours: 27 Bangladeshi Muslims, nine Bangladeshi Hindus, and nine people from the Bawm tribal community. They then merged these results with published data from around the world, for a final dataset of 2,217 people. Each person’s DNA was read at about 370,000 key places along the genome, where nucleotide letters commonly differ between people.

articles.title: Israel army says it completed ground operation in central Gaza
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: Israel's military said that a ground operation involving tanks in central Gaza that began the previous day despite a U.S.-brokered ceasefire had come to an end on Thursday (November 19, 2026).

The Defence Ministry's body in charge of civilian affairs in Palestinian territories, Coordinator of Government Activities in the Territories (COGAT), said in a statement that Palestinians would again be free to move in the targeted areas near the Al-Bureij and Nuseirat refugee camps.

"We would like to inform you that the activity has ended, and the Salah al-Din axis has been reopened," COGAT said in an Arabic-language statement on Facebook, referring to the war-shattered territory's main thoroughfare.

On Wednesday (November 18, 2026), the Israeli military said it had launched an operation in a Hamas-controlled area of central Gaza, beyond the so-called "Yellow Line" which separates areas under Israeli military and Hamas control following an October 2025 ceasefire.
An AFP journalist reported seeing Israeli tanks positioning themselves east of the Nuseirat refugee camp.
Hamas denounced a "blatant ceasefire violation," while the military said the rare ground incursion was a response to Hamas ceasefire violations in the area.
The military said in a statement that the operation had been launched to "dismantle a terror tunnel west of the Yellow Line that posed an immediate and direct threat to IDF troops".

A Gaza security source told AFP there had been "intense Israeli artillery shelling" north of Nuseirat refugee camp and reported Israeli military vehicles in central Gaza "amid ongoing gunfire and airstrikes since midday".
Israel and Hamas regularly accuse each other of violating the U.S.-brokered ceasefire deal that came after two years of devastating war sparked by Hamas's October 7, 2023 attack on Israel.

More than 1,600 Palestinians have been killed since the start of the ceasefire, according to an AFP tally based on data from the Gaza Health Ministry, which operates under Hamas authority and whose figures are considered reliable by the United Nations.
Over the same period, the Israeli military says seven of its soldiers have been killed, as well as one civilian contractor.

articles.title: COP31 negotiators publish revised deal draft with no mention of fossil fuels
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: Climate negotiators stripped out any reference to ‌ending the use of fossil fuels in a slimmed-down draft deal text published ​on Thursday (November 19, 2026), as the COP31 meeting in Antalya, Turkiye, approaches its Friday (November 20, 2026) deadline.

The talks are ⁠taking place at a time when war and rising living costs are competing for the attention of policymakers and the public against the warming climate and its increasingly severe effects, including heatwaves, floods and droughts.

The revised deal, ‌which is not expected to be the final version, was weaker on some of the conference's central topics — fossil fuels, electrification and adaptation finance — compared to a first draft ‌published on Monday (November 16, 2026).

Monday's (November 16, 2026) two references to fossil fuels and limiting their use — a topic that ‌deeply ⁠divides nations in the negotiations every year — were removed, as was mention of a $120 ⁠billion target for finance to help developing countries adapt to climate change.
"This new text has gone backwards from the one released earlier in the week," said Mohamed Adow, director of climate and energy think tank Power Shift Africa.
"If this version of ​the text remains, it will be a ‌ghost COP. The summit will have nothing to show for what happened here."

Thursday's (November 19, 2026) draft did retain an acknowledgement that global warming could exceed the 1.5 degrees Celsius threshold countries have sought to preserve, and the need for "deep, rapid and sustained" cuts to greenhouse gas emissions.
It also encouraged efforts ‌to scale up the deployment of technologies that can suck carbon out of the atmosphere, something ​scientists say would be needed to bring temperatures back down.

Australia, which is leading negotiations under a split presidency arrangement with Turkiye, previously ⁠said Monday's (November 16, 2026) opening draft of the deal was always intended to be a broad document that would then be narrowed down.

While the conference is scheduled to end on Friday (November 20, 2026), in recent years, efforts to secure ‌consensus among the nearly 200 countries participating have regularly blown past this deadline by more than 24 hours.
The need to limit rising global temperatures is widely accepted by participants, but they don't all agree on the best way to do so, who should pay for it, and how quickly the world needs to act.

Thursday's (November 19, 2026) draft deal also called for "global cooperation" to boost electricity’s share of world energy consumption to 35% by 2035, up from around 23% now — something proponents say would slash greenhouse gas emissions ‌by reducing fossil fuel use.

articles.title: Third Ukrainian strike in 4 days halts rail traffic on Russia's Kerch Bridge to Crimea
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: A third Ukrainian aerial attack in four days on the key Kerch Bridge linking Russia to Russian-held Crimea halted rail traffic across the span, officials said Thursday (November 19, 2026), after earlier strikes shut down the road section of the landmark that is a symbol of Moscow's invasion.
Train traffic across the bridge stopped after the overnight strike while authorities assessed the damage, but it resumed in the afternoon, according to Russian state news agency RIA Novosti .

The Ukrainian strikes seemed calculated to embarrass Russian President Vladimir Putin as he met in China with President Xi Jinping and U.S. President Donald Trump, as well as to demonstrate that Kyiv still holds cards in the war and to undermine Russia's argument that its victory is inevitable.

The attack came hours before the start of talks in Berlin between U.S. envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy alongside more than 40 European leaders who are supporting Ukraine's war effort and fear being sidelined by Mr. Trump's direct talks with Mr. Putin.
“We will respond to these attacks, and I want everyone to be clear about that,” Mr. Putin told reporters in Shenzhen, China.
He insisted the bridge is a civilian asset, adding that he had ordered the bridge closed to the transport of military hardware or ammunition.
Mr. Putin also said that the road side of the bridge had been “seriously damaged” but vowed to rebuild it.
The rail section is believed to be stronger than the road side, to bear the greater weight of cargo wagons.

The 19-kilometre (12-mile) Kerch Bridge is a key route for military and civilian supplies to Crimea, which Moscow seized in defiance of international law in 2014 and uses to support front-line troops. It is a potent reminder of Russia's illegal annexation of the territory and has been a prime target for Ukraine.

A large section of the road deck and an arch collapsed in the culmination of weeks of preparatory strikes over seven stages of the operation, according to Mr. Zelenskyy, and the train track was damaged by domestically produced Neptune missiles, Ukraine's Defence Ministry said.
Now Russia will need to reroute fuel and ammunition supplies over land, where “our drones are waiting for the cargo,” the ministry said.
The Russian Defence Ministry said on Thursday (November 19, 2026) that its air defences intercepted 53 Ukrainian drones over 10 Russian regions during the night.

articles.title: How U.S. controls flow of advanced tech, chip, and compute to China | Explained
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Updates, Tech & Climate Reports
fullParagraphs: The story so far: The battle for the most sought after commodity that underpins development of artificial intelligence technology just grew fiercer after the U.S. Commerce Department, on November 16, 2026, issued an interim final rule (IFR) barring data centre operators outside of the U.S., equipped with advanced American AI chips, from providing cloud service to businesses in two dozen countries, including China, Iran and Russia. The new, yet to be published, rule also restricts American companies from freely shipping high-end AI chips to a set of five countries, including Indonesia, Malaysia, and Singapore, without the explicit approval of the U.S. government.

China has censured the move, calling it “yet another case of the U.S. overstretching the concept of national security, and abusing export control measures to interfere in normal trade and tech cooperation between China and other countries and go after China’s high-tech industry.”
The interim rule came just days ahead of the meeting between U.S. President Donald Trump and China’s President Xi Jinping in Shenzhen, China on the sidelines of the November 18-19 APEC Summit.

The U.S. government’s policy on making advanced technology inaccessible to China has been a talking point among lawmakers in Washington for well over a decade, but a legal tool to control the flow took shape only during the first Trump term when the administration passed the Export Control Reform Act in 2018.

It gave the U.S. a legal weapon to control the movement of advanced technology originating from the country. Its primary purpose was to curb export of top-tier chips that had dual-use — both commercial and military purposes — to countries like China, Russia and Iran.

articles.title: Hyderabad doctor brings down rare disease drug cost from ₹9 crore to ₹2.5 lakh; seven children to get free treatment
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Updates, Tech & Climate Reports
fullParagraphs: Imagine having a medicine that could help manage your child’s rare genetic condition, but being unable to afford it because a year’s treatment costs as much as ₹9 crore. For seven families in India, that situation could soon change.

Seven children diagnosed with Allan-Herndon-Dudley syndrome (AHDS), a rare genetic disorder, are set to receive a year’s supply of the medicine tiratricol free of cost on November 30, following an initiative led by Hyderabad-based paediatrician Dr. Sivaranjani Santosh and Access to Medicines India.

The development is significant not just because the families will receive the medicine without paying for it, but also because its cost has been brought down through pharmaceutical compounding in the Netherlands. While the commercial version of the drug costs approximately ₹4.68 crore to ₹9 crore per child annually, the compounded formulation is estimated to cost just ₹2.5 lakh per child for a year.

The medicine has been prepared by Transvaal Pharmacy in The Hague, Netherlands, with support from the Netherlands-based Pharmaceutical Accountability Foundation (PAF). The first batch will be handed over to the parents of the seven children along with the necessary documentation and individual import permissions. The families have secured approvals for one year of treatment. As the compounded medicine has a shelf life of six months, it will be imported in two batches.

The initiative began after Arav, a child under the care of Dr. Sivaranjani, was diagnosed with AHDS, also known as MCT8 deficiency. The condition is caused by mutations affecting the MCT8 gene, which plays an important role in transporting thyroid hormones into brain cells. Tiratricol, also known as TRIAC, acts on thyroid hormone receptors and may help overcome some effects of the deficiency. It also helps minimise complications associated with peripheral thyrotoxicosis.

Although the medicine was available in Europe, its commercial price put it beyond the reach of most Indian families. Arav’s mother, Pavitra Sirolkar, had to arrange approximately ₹12 lakh to ₹13 lakh for just one month’s supply of the medicine from Germany. Dr. Sivaranjani initially approached paediatricians, endocrinologists and paediatric neurologists to explore ways of procuring the drug. Doctors at Christian Medical College (CMC), Vellore, where five other children with the same condition had been identified, were also approached.

Attempts to obtain the medicine through pharmaceutical company Egetis Therapeutics and its compassionate-use programme did not succeed. The situation eventually prompted Dr. Sivaranjani to take the issue to social media. On September 7, she posted an appeal seeking help for the family and urged people to tag the Prime Minister, Union Health Minister and other government representatives. The appeal gained attention, bringing it to the notice of PAF.

The foundation subsequently explored the possibility of preparing the medicine through pharmaceutical compounding using the active pharmaceutical ingredient. Transvaal Pharmacy conducted test batches and developed a formulation for the seven children. The initial group included Arav and five children receiving treatment at CMC Vellore. A seventh child, aged one year, was identified after his father contacted Dr Sivaranjani following her social media appeal.

According to PAF, the total cost of providing one year’s treatment to all seven children is €14,200, approximately ₹15.08 lakh. Of this, Dr Sivaranjani raised approximately ₹6.09 lakh in India, while PAF undertook to raise the remaining €8,600, approximately ₹9.13 lakh, in the Netherlands. The medicine will be provided to all seven families free of cost.

While the November 30 handover addresses the immediate treatment requirements of the seven children, Dr. Sivaranjani believes that importing the medicine cannot be a permanent solution. She plans to approach the Union government and work with Access to Medicines India and other organisations to explore the possibility of getting the medicine compounded in India and making it accessible to more children.

“How can a medicine be available in the world but not be available for our children? We should get the medicine compounded in India and make it available for all the children with this condition,” she said.

articles.title: Why data interoperability is critical to the future of hospital care
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Updates, Tech & Climate Reports
fullParagraphs: In an intensive care unit, every second matters. A critically ill patient may be connected to several devices, including patient monitors, ventilators and infusion pumps, while laboratory systems and electronic health records continuously generate additional information. Together, these systems create a large and rapidly-changing picture of the patient’s condition. However, when the information remains fragmented across devices and platforms, clinicians may spend valuable time locating, verifying and reconciling data before they can act.

This makes interoperability a clinical priority in critical care, not simply an information technology requirement. Integration enables systems to exchange data, but true interoperability ensures that the information being exchanged is accurate, interpretable and clinically relevant. This can help care teams coordinate and prioritise interventions more effectively while reducing the need to move between multiple systems to assemble a clinical picture.

fullParagraphs: The wait is over. ‌After 13 years and an estimated $1 billion or more in production costs, the most anticipated video game release in history is finally ​here.

“Grand Theft Auto VI” became available as midnight struck in New Zealand on Thursday (November 19, 2026), with the launch then following the clock around ⁠the world. Millions of players have already downloaded the game to their consoles in anticipation.

The release, with events worldwide and many users taking days off work to play, marks the latest instalment in one of entertainment’s most successful franchises. Since its 1997 debut, “Grand Theft Auto” has become one of the best-selling video game series of all time.

“I’ve been waiting 13 years to ‌play,” said 20-year-old Jonah Bowen-Brown from Australia’s southern island of Tasmania, who persuaded his mother to give him and his brother a week off work at the family-run fragrance shop, Whiff-it!.
“She was really against it at first,” said Bowen-Brown. “I had to say, mum, please, please, I need ‌it.”
A gamer plays Grand Theft Auto VI in Miami, Florida | Photo Credit: Reuters
The game is made by Take-Two Interactive’s Rockstar Games and available on Sony’s PlayStation 5 and Microsoft’s Xbox Series X and S consoles.

The original “Grand Theft ‌Auto” ⁠looks basic by today’s standards, and its missions — stealing cars and carrying out jobs for crime syndicates — angered politicians and parents. But it delighted ⁠gamers.

Each successive release delivered more sophisticated graphics and storytelling. “Grand Theft Auto V”, released in 2013 and set in the fictional Los Santos, a stand-in for Los Angeles, became one of the best-selling video games ever.
While retaining the series’ trademark mix of crime, driving and morally dubious missions, it added activities ranging from parachute jumps to cinema visits and radio stations satirising US culture.
The action now moves to Vice City, a ‌fictional version of Miami, in the state of Leonida, the game’s take on Florida.

From previews, fans know a little. Play will switch between two leading characters, Lucia Caminos and Jason Duval. They are partners in crime and romantically involved — just how romantically will be up to the player. There will be nightclubs, gun stores, scuba diving and a zoo. But much remains to be revealed.

fullParagraphs: Each year, the summits of the 11-member Association of South-East Asian Nations mark an important moment on the diplomatic calendar: India is able to interact with all of its partners in the Indo-Pacific and engage global powers at the ASEAN-India Summit and the East Asia Summit. Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s talks with Indo-Pacific players focused on a future shaped “not by competition, but by cooperation”. This year, the summit in Manila hosted by the Philippines had many other imperatives. These were the first ASEAN summits since the U.S.-Israel attacks on Iran and Iran’s Hormuz blockade and strikes on Gulf countries that have upended energy and trade across South and South East Asia. Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s call for “peace, stability, and predictability” in the world during the EAS was aimed as much at leaders from the U.S., Russia and China as it was for the region. The visit had a bilateral context — the Philippines and India have intensified ties considerably in the past year, since the visit of President Bongbong Marcos to Delhi in August 2025, including the upgradation of the Strategic Partnership, maritime exchanges and negotiations over the supply of more Indian-made Brahmos missile battery systems to the Philippines. This year, after months of concerns about U.S. President Donald Trump’s lack of interest in the Quad grouping, the U.S. decided to host a summit of U.S.-India-Australia-Japan Quad leaders on the side-lines of the ASEAN summits, the first time the summit has been held in a non-Quad country.

Given the stakes, there were several outcomes from all the three summits that PM Modi attended back-to-back on Tuesday — the ASEAN India Summit launched a new cooperation on disaster management, and the East Asia Summit focused on countering cyber-crime. PM Modi’s announcement that India would give all ASEAN citizens free tourist visas is expected to increase people-to-people interactions and trade. At the Quad summit, President Trump made a number of announcements including the launch of a Quad Business leaders forum, to be held in Mumbai next year, and the first Quad naval exercises with patrol aircraft. However, the outcomes in Manila paled in significance to the anticipation over Mr. Trump’s next stop in Shenzhen for the Asia Pacific Economic Conference (APEC), with an unprecedented three-way summit with Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping planned on Thursday. New Delhi must watch the outcomes of that summit among the “global superpowers” much more closely.

articles.title: Testing times: On India’s two-Test series against New Zealand
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: New Zealand at home remains an indomitable cricketing opposition. Even the great West Indian squad led by Clive Lloyd suffered a 0-1 Test series defeat in 1980. Pitches that look lush as English meadows, the wind that is often bone-chilling cold, and fast bowlers relishing their prospects, make any tour of New Zealand a difficult outing. So far, the visiting Indians have done well, having won the T20I and ODI series, but the real contest starts with the first Test at Wellington’s Basin Reserve from Thursday. The Shubman Gill-led men’s last overseas tour of Sri Lanka ended with a middling 1-0 victory in the two Tests, but more needs to be done against New Zealand in the latest two-Test series. Placed fourth in the ICC World Test Championship (WTC) table, and with hopes of securing a final berth seemingly fragile, India is in a win-all-games situation first up against New Zealand and later when Australia arrives next year. Against current WTC topper New Zealand, the Indian batters have to stay anchored. This is a line-up that no longer has Rohit Sharma, Virat Kohli, Cheteshwar Pujara and Ajinkya Rahane. Gill and company get another opportunity to reiterate their credentials.

For some rugged inspiration they need not look beyond coach Gautam Gambhir in their dressing room. The doughty former India opener batted for 643 minutes while scoring a match-saving 137 in the Napier Test during the 2009 tour. The southpaw will be hoping that the current batting unit, which is high on flair, will remain sober and effectively counter the host. K.L. Rahul, Yashasvi Jaiswal, Devdutt Padikkal and Gill have the onerous task of negating the New Zealand seamers in their backyard. Rishabh Pant and Dhruv Jurel add depth, and if the former can successfully unleash his maverick batting approach, India can upset the host’s best-laid plans. New Zealand will miss the retired Kane Williamson but its batters would be comfortable on familiar surfaces. For India, much would hinge on how Jasprit Bumrah bowls. If the spearhead clicks, then it becomes easier for much of his support-cast that includes the persevering Mohammed Siraj, who was a touch rusty in Sri Lanka. From the squads of the past to the present unit, Ravindra Jadeja remains the link. Whether he will get a role to play or whether the management prefers an all-pace attack, remains a matter of conjecture. The home team led by Tom Latham will depend on Matt Henry, Kyle Jameson and other pacers, to choke the Indian batters. A hard task awaits India, first at Wellington and then at Christchurch.

articles.title: Elusive peace: On Kashmir terror attack
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: Three months of lull established by security forces in Jammu and Kashmir was rattled by the back-to-back incidents of violence in the past six days. On November 11, a terror attack on a checkpoint manned by the personnel of the Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF) in Kulgam left three jawans injured. On November 16, a local, whom the police suspected of having joined the terror ranks a few days ago, was killed after six days of a siege-like anti-terror operation in residential areas of Kulgam. In Jammu’s Kishtwar, two Special Police Officers (SPOs) of the J&K Police were found dead with bullet wounds, a day after they were reported missing in a forest range on November 11. The police and the Army, however, remain tight-lipped about the circumstances around the killing of these SPOs, and there are conflicting reports on the circumstances that led to their deaths. The anti-terror operation in civilian areas of Kulgam has raised concerns. Former J&K Chief Minister and PDP president Mehbooba Mufti described the operation, spread over six days, as “collective punishment that only breeds alienation and resentment,” while NC spokesman Imran Nabi Dar suggested that entire villages were put under prolonged restrictions for days. The Omar Abdullah government , because of limited powers and no jurisdiction over the police in J&K, a Union Territory since 2019, finds itself hamstrung. The iron hand policy to stamp out terrorism and separatism has been effective from a strictly security perspective — terror attacks as well as local recruitments into terror ranks have declined. According to the police, local recruits have come down to single digit or fewer than 10 in Kashmir.

That said, the decline in terrorist incidents and the silence of the streets should not be mistaken for peace. The current situation demands a political reach-out by the Centre to all the stakeholders of J&K. It has to begin with the much-promised restoration of Statehood , which will give the voters a sense that their mass participation in the 2024 Assembly elections allowed their elected leaders to hold institutions accountable, and they were able to work freely to protect the interests of the region. Though the security agencies need to be focused on Pakistan-backed terrorism, it should not come at the cost of re-inflicting psychological scars within Kashmir, which could turn into a powder keg if left unattended. Healing through both political and security processes has to be complementary rather than conflicting. Allowing the political class of J&K to establish its writ and providing room to security agencies to combat challenges are not contradictory.

articles.title: All-too fallible: On India’s vote against moratorium on death penalty
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: India’s vote against a proposed global moratorium on the death penalty at the UN is consistent with its position at the forum; it has defended its retention of the penalty as a sovereign decision backed by judicial safeguards, including the “rarest of rare” condition and sessions courts’ sentences requiring a High Court’s confirmation. At the same time, the Supreme Court has increasingly restricted capital punishment and research has failed to find evidence of additional deterrence over life imprisonment . India’s distinction between judicial executions and extrajudicial killings is legally valid but its further claim that due process protects people facing execution is less so. While India last executed convicts in 2020, for the Delhi gang-rape and murder, Parliament expanded the number of capital offences under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita — a form of penal populism that projects the political attractiveness of the state’s response to public outrage, especially in cases of sexual violence, without addressing the poor policing and low conviction rates that actually undermine deterrence . The country had 574 people on death row on December 31, 2025, the highest since 2016, thanks to trial court rulings, challenging claims about judicial safeguards in practice. The report of the 2015 Law Commission headed by Justice A.P. Shah said the death penalty “fails to achieve any constitutionally valid penological goals” and recommended abolishing it for all crimes except terrorism and waging war.

Only a small group of countries worldwide are executing more people. In India, per Project 39A, the Supreme Court released 38 persons from death row in 2016-2025 after they had spent eight years there on average. Some have endured more than two decades. The punishment requires a measure of infallibility that the criminal justice system cannot supply. The safeguards neither deter convictions in cases with flawed evidence, false testimony, and so on nor remedy unequal access to competent legal representation among those facing the penalty. India should formally suspend executions and commission a review of penalty statutes and the treatment of prisoners on death row. Second, it should spare offences that do not involve intentional killing from the penalty. Research suggests meting out excessively harsh punishments for non-fatal crimes could incentivise offenders to escalate their violence, including to kill potential witnesses. The greater goal should be to abolish the practice in law while improving investigative and prosecutorial practices and access to legal aid.

articles.title: Outlook outage: On Microsoft and dangers of centralising digital systems
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: Last week, Microsoft’s suite of productivity and email software, which businesses, governments, hospitals and a host of other organisations rely upon round-the-clock, abruptly stopped working globally , affecting tens of millions of people around the world. The company has cited a network upgrade gone awry as the root cause of the incident. Incidents such as the Microsoft 365 outage are a natural consequence of businesses and governments allowing key digital systems to become centralised all over the world. The internet remains, and was pioneered as, a network of networks. If one business’s networks went down, the reasoning went, others would not fall like dominos: everyone was, after all, connected to everyone else. But the economics have long been prohibitive, with dedicated servers and web-connected infrastructure infeasible for all but the largest businesses, with even those firms seeking the enticing cost savings from socialised infrastructure. That made sense: the internet made shared infrastructure more economical, allowing hardware and maintenance costs to be spread so far and wide that at a per-user level prices have been negligible. Competition among major cloud providers, the few that remain at Microsoft’s scale, have kept prices affordable for enterprise software for all shades of organisations.

Digital services have grown more sophisticated, and more deeply integrated into the economy as this centralisation unfolded. But the downside is that, regardless of the sophistication and professionalism of any company, mistakes happen, and the scale of these mistakes can quickly cascade over to the entire economy. There are societal and organisational lessons to be gleaned from these episodes. There is no such thing as a reliable vendor. Governments must also draw a cyber sovereignty lesson here that does not simply entail swapping a global vendor for a domestic one. It is the subversion of the internet’s architecture that is at the root of these incidents. Investing in resilience — and shielding critical operations from destabilising disruptions, no matter how improbable — should inform attitudes to digital systems. As a new generation of AI data centres is poised to supercharge the centralised systems of yesteryear, it is all the more imperative to mitigate even occasional vagaries of large systems.

But the downside is that, regardless of the sophistication and professionalism of any company, mistakes happen, and the scale of these mistakes can quickly cascade over to the entire economy. There are societal and organisational lessons to be gleaned from these episodes. There is no such thing as a reliable vendor. Governments must also draw a cyber sovereignty lesson here that does not simply entail swapping a global vendor for a domestic one. It is the subversion of the internet’s architecture that is at the root of these incidents. Investing in resilience — and shielding critical operations from destabilising disruptions, no matter how improbable — should inform attitudes to digital systems. As a new generation of AI data centres is poised to supercharge the centralised systems of yesteryear, it is all the more imperative to mitigate even occasional vagaries of large systems.

articles.title: Clear the path: On SCO Civilisational Dialogue Forum in New Delhi
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: While maintaining its hard stance on cross-border terrorism, India has an opportunity to recognise that many of its other interests still merit sustained cooperation with Pakistan as the latter’s climate minister Musadik Masood Malik prepares to attend the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Civilisational Dialogue Forum in New Delhi. India’s official position since the Pahalgam attack and the ensuing confrontations along the border is that terrorism and bilateral talks cannot coexist. A month later, Prime Minister Narendra Modi signalled that India’s relations with Pakistan would remain subordinate to its demands on cross-border terrorism by extending the condition to trade and water. South Asia is already one of the least economically integrated regions worldwide, with intra-regional trade at around 5%, and, as Chatham House has inferred, strained ties between India and its neighbours have created diplomatic vacuums that Beijing has taken advantage of through trilateral and regional groupings. Now, by inviting all SCO members to the national capital and participating in meetings ahead of the August 2027 Islamabad Summit, New Delhi has shown some maturity as a convening power. Islamabad is also being pragmatic in keeping channels open during its SCO chairmanship by participating in an initiative championed by Mr. Modi.

The pursuit of regionwide water security remains particularly fluid, with India seemingly overlooking the fact that it is upstream of Pakistan and Bangladesh and downstream of China. After India stopped sharing routine hydrological data of the Indus river and approved the Chenab-Beas link tunnel project, Mr. Malik fanned the flames saying Pakistan would “cut off those hands” seeking to restrict its share of the water. Yet China has now restricted the same data vis-à-vis the Brahmaputra while it builds the Medog mega-dam in Tibet. India has also protested the proposed Padma Barrage in Bangladesh, which has been increasing its alignment with China, echoing India building the Farakka Barrage over East Pakistan’s objections in 1961. Climate change is rendering cooperation more essential to manage the integrity of contested geographies, the willingness of border populations to engage, and the potential to generate hydroelectric power. New Delhi should retreat from the notion that working together on the Indus will be a concession to Islamabad and see in the Dialogue an opportunity to restore the necessary channels. Suspending ties may communicate political resolve but will not diminish terrorists’ capabilities in the region or improve India’s security. It has already compromised India’s ambitions to regional leadership, which require the ability to keep engaging even with difficult neighbours. India should go beyond using multilateral fora to assert its national position and start identifying areas where bilateral cooperation serves its interests, including with Pakistan.

articles.title: UDF govt. smacks of corruption and nepotism: Keralam BJP general secretary
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: The BJP on Wednesday accused the V.D. Satheesan-led UDF government, which completed six months in office, of corruption, nepotism and betrayal of youth. The UDF government has amply demonstrated that it lacked collective responsibility and coordination in the honeymoon period itself, the BJP State general secretary, S. Suresh, said here on Wednesday.

Addressing media persons here, Mr. Suresh said that the six-month-old UDF Government was a failure and that it is no different from the Left government that ruled the State for the last ten years. “The only difference is that Mr. Satheesan does whatever Mr. Pinarayi Vijayan did, but with a smile,” he said.
He alleged that the government in charge now was a “communal” government, whose policies were being shaped by the Indian Union Muslim League and Jamaat-e-Islami.

The government, he said, had not implemented the five “Indira Guarantees” on which it came to power. He said free bus travel for women had been only partially implemented and that the promises of ₹25-lakh health insurance, welfare pension of ₹3,000 and interest-free loans of ₹5 lakh for the youth were conveniently forgotten

Mr. Suresh said that the government initially refused to act on allegations of serious irregularities in Kerala Public Service Commission appointments and of political backdoor recruitment. He claimed that the government was forced into ordering a Vigilance inquiry only after the BJP took up the matter with the Governor, who in turn sent a report to the President.

He flayed the Government of forfeiting thousands of crores in Central aid by opting out of PH SHRI scheme, which would have gone into the infrastructure building of government schools and alleged that the UDF government took this decision to appease IUML and Jammat-e- Islami. He also criticised the withdrawal of approval for the Mayilpeeli scholarship on political grounds

He alleged that the government was in total disarray, with its constituent parties in total dissent with the Chief Minister. The UDF convenor seemed to have no knowledge of the decisions of the government, while the KPCC president, who was also a Minister, did not even know the decisions taken in his own department by the Chief Minister. He said that the BJP will continue a strong fight against the UDF government with the same intensity it showed against the Pinarayi government.

Keralam Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan is inventing interpretations as a face-saver to cover up the total collapse of collective responsibility of the State cabinet, according to CPI State secretary Binoy Viswam. The highlight of the cabinet meeting held on the day the UDF government completed six months in office was the dispute between the Chief Minister and the Ministers over all important issues. Serious disputes marred the discussions including those on the appointments to the State Public Service Commission and Devaswom Board.

When prominent leaders of the Congress publicly speak about a lack of consultation either in the party or the coalition, naturally that gets reflected in the cabinet as well. He called the Chief Minister ‘thick-skinned’ for defending the situation as the ‘beauty of democracy’, said Mr. Viswam.

articles.title: Commonwealth meet focuses on women’s leadership, tech-driven challenges, destigmatising menopause
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: The two-day Commonwealth Women Parliamentarians (CWP) India Region meet in Bengaluru concluded on Wednesday, with discussions focused on women’s leadership, technology-driven challenges and destigmatising menopause.

Participating in the valedictory session, Karnataka Governor Sudha Yadav said democracy can truly be complete only when women participate equally and actively in decision-making, and that women and men should work as equal partners to achieve the fullest progress of society. “Women’s leadership brings strength to democracy, sensitivity to governance and a transformative vision to nation-building. Empowerment must go beyond providing opportunities to ensuring that women’s voices are heard, their perspectives valued and their leadership recognised in decision-making,” she said.

According to Commonwealth Women Parliamentarians India Region Chairperson D. Purandeshwari, focused discussions took place on menopause and women’s health issues, and efforts would be made to destigmatise them. She also stressed the need to find solutions to online attacks on women.

Rajya Sabha Deputy Chairman Harivansh Narayan Singh said protecting the dignity of women was crucial to strengthening their participation in politics. “Cyberstalking, deepfakes and AI-based attacks are seriously affecting women. There is a need to create awareness about the law and ensure its effective implementation,” he said.

The two-day event witnessed discussions on technology empowering women in education, health and finance, while also exposing them to cyberstalking, phishing, deepfakes and AI-driven harassment that deter women from entering public life. Suggestions were made to integrate AI directly into social media platforms to prevent the spread of misinformation and harmful content.

Discussions also focused on training women lawmakers in policymaking, public finance and programme implementation, as well as bridging the digital divide to bring more women from rural India into legislative spaces.

The conference saw the participation of 100 delegates, including women Members of Parliament (MPs) and Members of Legislative Assemblies (MLAs), alongside international representatives such as UN Women representative Shoko Ishikawa of Japan and CWP African Region Chairperson and Malawi MP Grace Kwelepeta.

articles.title: West Bengal CM to take action in the missionary school dress code row, says State BJP head
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: West Bengal Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) president Samik Bhattacharya has said that he has brought the matter involving a teacher at a reputed Christian missionary school in Kolkata questioned for wearing a saffron saree to the notice of State’s Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari.

“I have told the Chief Minister. He will take whatever action is required,” Mr. Bhattacharya told media persons. The BJP leader reiterated that he has not said anything baseless and those who were supposed to get the message have got it.

The State BJP president alleged that religious conversions by Christian groups are increasing in certain tribal areas of the State including Purba Bardhaman, Asansol and Kalimpong. “This will not continue. Babur’s rule is no more here. Our fight is against religious conversion,” he said.

Mr. Bhattacharya on November 15 had issued a warning to Christian missionary schools in the State raising the issue of a teacher being questioned for putting on saffron saree. The BJP Rajya Sabha MP had also claimed that religious conversions are on the rise in the State. The remark had triggered strong reaction from Christian groups, who have been vocal about the attacks on churches and house prayer gatherings.

Asked about the allegations made by the BJP president on November 15 Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari on Tuesday (November 17, 2026) had said the State government would take action against any individual or withdraw the no-objection certificate of an institution if allegations of a Christian missionary school restricting a staffer from wearing a saffron saree were found to be true.

“I will verify the information. If it is true and there is a written complaint against an individual, then action will be taken against the individual. If the institution is involved in something like this, its NOC (no-objection certificate) will be withdrawn,” Mr. Adhikari said.
Meanwhile, Bangiya Christiya Pariseba, an organisation working for Christians in the State raised certain questions in the wake of remarks made by the BJP president.

“Why is no legal action being taken against actual perpetrators? If illegal religious conversions are indeed taking place, why are the specific individuals responsible not being identified and prosecuted under the law? Does this reluctance indicate an unwillingness to let the truth come out?” a press statement by the organisation said.

The statement by Surbir Sarkar, State working president of BCP said that why was the BJP president or the State government silent on vigilante attacks when these groups that are repeatedly taking the law into their own hands to launch brutal attacks and vandalise peaceful prayer meetings.

articles.title: Plea in SC asks how many voters have filled enumeration forms to get back on electoral rolls
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: A fresh petition has been filed in the Supreme Court seeking disclosure of the number of Delhi voters whose names were deleted from the draft electoral rolls under the absent, shifted, dead and duplicate (ASDD) categories but who subsequently submitted enumeration forms to be restored to the voter list.
The petitioners have also sought an extension of the provision allowing such voters to submit enumeration forms and the restoration of their old Electoral Photo Identity Card (EPIC) numbers.

Filed on Tuesday (November 17, 2026) by transparency rights activists Anjali Bharadwaj and Amrita Johri, the petition argues that ASDD voters who have already submitted Form 6 should also be allowed to fill enumeration forms.

This, they said, would ensure that they are restored to the electoral rolls with their existing EPIC numbers instead of being classified as new voters. Form 6 is intended for registering new voters but had also been used by those whose names were deleted during the Special Intensive Revision (SIR).

During an earlier hearing, the Supreme Court had termed the use of Form 6 by voters excluded from the draft rolls under the ASDD category an “error”, as the form requires applicants to declare that they are first-time voters.

Subsequently, the Election Commission of India issued a directive allowing voters marked as ASDD in seven States, including Delhi, where the SIR is under way, to submit enumeration forms again instead of using Form 6. These voters had been excluded because their issued enumeration forms were not received back.
The petition has also raised concerns over the alleged misuse of Form 7 for targeted deletions. It has sought an audit and public disclosure of all Form 7 applications submitted so far.

The petitioners have further requested that booth-level agents (BLAs) of political parties filing Form 7 be required to identify themselves as party representatives rather than submitting applications only under their individual names.

articles.title: Eknath Shinde tears Sonia Gandhi’s book over Savarkar references, seeks ban in Maharashtra
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: Shiv Sena’s Eknath Shinde on Wednesday (November 18, 2026) tore pages from Sonia Gandhi’s memoir ‘Belonging: A Journey of Love’, demanding that the publisher withdraw two pages that the party claimed contained objectionable references to Vinayak Damodar Savarkar.

“We have torn the pages of the book as a mark of protest against the statements on Savarkar ji. We have sought that Harper Collins, the publisher, should scrap these two pages. Till they do that, we have sought that the Maharashtra government ban the sale of the book in the State. We will soon write to the government to seek a ban,” Shiv Sena leader Sanjay Nirupam told The Hindu .
He was among the six party spokespersons who addressed a press conference on Wednesday (November 18, 2026). The Shiv Sena is part of the ruling Mahayuti alliance in Maharashtra.

The Congress hit back at the Sena, condemning the act as “shameful”. “It shows intellectual bankruptcy. I feel pity for them. When you spit at the sun, the spit lands on you. It is a condemnable act,” Maharashtra Congress president Harshawardhan Sapkal said.

Former Chief Minister Prithviraj Chavan termed the act “childish”. “We are not the Taliban. We believe in the Constitution of Babasaheb Ambedkar. Everyone has the right to express their opinion. If you do not accept her views or if you think there are factual inaccuracies, refute them or point them out or write a separate book. But tearing a book is childishness,” he said.

Meanwhile, Shiv Sena leader Shaina NC tore a photograph bearing the image of Balasaheb Thackeray during the press conference. When this was pointed out to her, she was seen slipping the torn photograph under a pile of papers. She later justified the act, saying that the photograph showed Balasaheb Thackeray slapping an effigy of Manishankar Aiyar with a chappal.

“This is what he has taught us. We have only torn the pages of a book,” she said. She was later summoned by Deputy Chief Minister Eknath Shinde. After the meeting, he said there was no question of anyone insulting Balasaheb Thackeray.
“He is venerable for us. Nobody can insult him,” Mr. Shinde said.

Meanwhile, the Uddhav Sena staged protests at several places in Maharashtra, including Mumbai. The issue also triggered a backlash in the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC), where Shiv Sena (UBT) leader Kishori Pednekar engaged in a heated exchange with Mumbai Mayor Ritu Tawde.
The Shiv Sena said the references to Savarkar appeared on pages 201 and 443 of the book.

“Derogatory words have been used for Veer Savarkar, portraying him as if he were some fascist. He is, in fact, a freedom fighter who struggled for India. We condemn this. Carrying forward the ideology of Hindu Hriday Samrat Balasaheb Thackeray, we only wish for a stable India where our freedom fighters are given the respect they deserve,” Ms. Shaina NC said.
Shiv Sena leaders questioned Mr. Uddhav Thackeray over his alliance with the Congress and asked how he could tolerate the alleged insult of the Hindutva ideologue.

articles.title: Bombay HC sets aside ICICI Bank Board of Directors’ sanction order on Chanda Kochhar
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: A sanction order, dated May 15, 2023, issued by the Board of Directors of ICICI Bank to prosecute Chanda Kochhar, was set aside by Justice Milind N. Jadhav of the Bombay High Court, who held that the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) constitutes the authority with jurisdiction under Section 36-AA(1) of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949, to grant permission.

Section 36-AA(1) of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949 states that the RBI possesses the power to remove a Chairperson, Director, or an officer from a bank, and because the power of removal vests with the RBI, the Board of Directors cannot act as the authority to grant sanction, the judge noted. The RBI did not pass an order of removal against the petitioner, and the petitioner had lost the opportunity to make a representation to the RBI against a removal order, Justice Jadhav said.

Justice Jadhav stated that nullity of sanction goes to the root of prosecution in proceedings under the Prevention of Corruption Act as it is a fact relating to jurisdiction and it stands on a pedestal as an absence of sanction, adding that the Board of Directors failed to examine evidence and material collected by the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) before granting permission.

The petitioner served as the Managing Director of ICICI Bank when the CBI registered a report in 2019 regarding loans sanctioned to the Videocon Group. The agency alleged that the petitioner had received an amount through a company where her husband served as a director, and that a flat was transferred to a Trust belonging to her husband. The petitioner filed a writ petition seeking to quash a sanction order dated May 15, 2023, granted under Section 19 of the Prevention of Corruption Act to prosecute her in a case registered by the CBI.

The petitioner argued that the Board of Directors of ICICI Bank does not possess the authority to grant sanction and that the RBI holds the power to remove an MD under the Banking Regulation Act. The advocate for the CBI argued that the Board of Directors held the power to appoint and remove an MD as per the Articles of Association, and that the question regarding the validity of sanction requires a trial and evidence for determination.

The court quashed and set aside the sanction granted by the Board of Directors, noting that the Board did not record the reasons in writing for the removal, and the document of sanction for prosecution issued by the Board dated May 15, 2023 did not constitute a sanction under Section 19(1)(c) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, resulting in the conclusion that cognisance taken by the court of the offence lacked basis relating to jurisdiction.

articles.title: India’s Oct. crude import bill soars 87.5% to $19.5-bn amid West Asia tensions, volumes up 11%
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: India’s crude oil import bill surged 87.5% year-on-year (YoY) to $19.5 billion in October, as elevated international benchmark prices, fuelled by renewed tensions in West Asia, sharply increased procurement costs. The increase came alongside an 11% rise in import volumes.

The net import bill, calculated as imports of crude oil, petroleum products and natural gas less exports of petroleum products, rose 60% to $16 billion during the month, compared with $10 billion in October last year.
Higher export realisations from petroleum products, however, provided some cushion against the escalating import burden.

According to provisional data released by the Petroleum Planning and Analysis Cell (PPAC), India imported 23.3 million metric tonnes (MMT) of crude oil in October, against 21 MMT in the corresponding month last year.
The expenditure on crude imports, meanwhile, climbed to $19.5 billion from $10.4 billion, reflecting the disproportionate impact of higher international prices on the country’s energy import bill.

The Indian crude oil basket averaged $119.91 per barrel in October, compared with $124.77 per barrel for Brent crude. In September, the Indian basket had averaged $116.09 per barrel, while Brent stood at $116.77 per barrel.

The sustained increase in benchmark prices, amid continuing geopolitical uncertainties in West Asia, has left India exposed to higher energy procurement costs, given its dependence on imported crude oil.
The impact of the rising crude import bill was partly offset by stronger earnings from petroleum product exports.
India’s petroleum product exports increased 5.9% in volume terms to 5.4 MMT in October. However, export revenues surged approximately 91% to $6.3 billion.
The increase in export earnings provided an important buffer against the higher cost of crude procurement.

Meanwhile, India’s liquefied natural gas (LNG) imports declined approximately 7% to 3,014 million standard cubic metres (MMSCM) during October. Despite the decline in volumes, the import bill increased 8.33%, pointing to the persistence of price pressures in the international gas market.

articles.title: India-U.S. trade deal signing will still ‘take some time’, says Commerce Secretary Rajesh Agrawal
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: The actual signing of the India-U.S. trade will still “take some time”, Commerce Secretary Rajesh Agrawal said on Wednesday (November 18, 2026), adding that the negotiation part and the legal text will be completed soon.

The delay in signing, he said, was because it can be done only after the U.S. concludes its Section 301 investigations into its trade partners and finalises its tariff structure. A few days ago, Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal asserted that the U.S. has acknowledged that India will receive lower tariffs as compared to its competitors.

“This is a deal that has been announced in February, the contours have already been announced as part of the joint statement,” Mr. Agrawal said while speaking at the curtain raiser of the FICCI Annual General Meeting. “The legal agreement has also been negotiated and it is now in final stages and it will be concluded soon.”
He was referring to the joint statement between India and the U.S. in February that announced the framework of an interim deal on trade.

However, Mr. Agrawal explained that the “challenge” is that this framework was announced against the background of the executive tariffs system that the U.S. President Donald Trump had put in place. At the time, the tariff on India was 50%. Later in February, the U.S. Supreme Court struck down the legal foundation of these tariffs.

“Now a new tariff architecture is being created by the U.S.,” Mr. Agrawal explained. “So until that tariff architecture comes back in place, the signing of a deal is something that I think will take some time. But concluding the negotiations and having everything ready will be something that we will strive to achieve as soon as possible.”
In particular, Mr. Agrawal spoke about the investigations undertaken by the American administration under Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974.

One of these investigations, regarding forced labour, has been completed and a tariff of 10% has been levied on imports from India. The second investigation, looking into excess capacity, is yet to be completed and could come with further tariffs.

“There are certain 301 investigations which are already under review,” Mr. Agrawal said. “Those will also be coming to the fore in the next few weeks or months. You can’t have a deal until you have got uncertainty around multiple investigations which are already there.”

Separately, without mentioning the U.S. or any other country, Mr. Agrawal also asserted that trade deals can take a long time to conclude when parties try to maximise the benefits accruing to them rather than engaging in a spirit of compromise.

“Negotiations are always, to my mind, the art of what is possible,” the Commerce Secretary said. “You try to bring it together and keep it in a mutual win-win position because each party wants to go from the table as a victor and wants to showcase to its people that they have got something good for their business.”
As such, he explained that most agreements are not perfect, but instead involve an even trade-off where parties have simultaneously minimized their risk and also taken advantage of what they can.

“People’s plates are shrinking, and factories are being locked down. Yet, the Prime Minister’s only concern remains politics,” he said on X, accusing the government of failing to acknowledge people’s hardships or offer relief.

articles.title: Saudis prepare for Houthi war to last well into 2027
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: Saudi Arabia is preparing for war against Yemen's Houthis to stretch well into next year, doubling down despite setbacks on the battlefield in Yemen ​and attacks disrupting life at home, said two Western officials briefed by Saudis on the plans.

The renewed conflict has become the most active front in ‌the wider Iran war, killing and wounding thousands and displacing hundreds of thousands in Yemen while derailing ​Saudi Arabia's efforts to draw in non-oil investment and host global events.
Public messaging around the war has also ⁠slowly shifted in the kingdom, with greater acknowledgement of its impacts.

Saudi officials now foresee the campaign stretching on for up to six months, aiming to see gains on the ground by the kingdom's Yemeni allies before any negotiations with the Houthis, according to Western officials, who spoke on condition ‌of anonymity to discuss non-public conversations with Saudi counterparts.
A third source familiar with the Saudi plans confirmed the accounts. All three said a deal to end the wider Iran war could see the Yemen conflict draw down.

The ‌third source also said Riyadh believes that U.S. offensive support for Saudi operations in Yemen, which President Donald Trump's administration has ‌so ⁠far withheld, could help change the tide of the conflict, potentially allowing Saudi-backed forces to make the gains ⁠they want within weeks.
A Saudi Foreign Ministry official declined to comment on the views of Saudi officials as described by the Western officials.

Saudi Arabia first entered the Yemen conflict in 2015 at the head of an Arab coalition to try to restore Yemen's government to power after the Houthis seized the ​capital Sanaa and much of the country. They fought to ‌a bloody stalemate and in 2022 reached a ceasefire that lasted until summer this year.

Since fighting restarted, the Houthis have seized the Red Sea coast and strategic Bab el-Mandeb strait from Saudi-backed forces, and encircled the city of Taiz in highlands above the government's temporary capital Aden on the southern coast.
Yemeni government forces mounted a counterattack last month, recapturing territory around the ‌strait, but withdrew over the past weekend to protect Aden in a major setback.

Saudi and Yemeni forces are ​now reorganising, with plans to protect Aden from the Houthi advances and potentially shift their offensive to eastern fronts where they have made some advances or have at least held their lines, according to one of the ⁠Western officials.

Saudi Arabia announced on Monday (November 16, 2026) it had replaced the commander overseeing the Saudi-led coalition. Yemen's government is also expected to reshuffle its military leadership, according to two people familiar with its plans.

articles.title: Ethiopia, Eritrea amass forces along border, heightening war fears: Sources
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: Ethiopia and Eritrea have amassed forces along their shared border, conflict monitors and people tied to militias in northern Ethiopia's Tigray ‌region said, fuelling fears of outright war between the historical rivals.

The build-up along the border has brought ​the two armies within striking distance of each other, according to the conflict monitors ACLED and the International ⁠Crisis Group, a person close to a pro-Ethiopian government militia in Tigray, and another person close to anti-government rebels there.

Reuters could not independently confirm reports of skirmishes between Ethiopian and Eritrean forces along the border. ACLED and a person close to the rebels said the ‌two sides had clashed in recent days, which would be their first direct armed exchanges in over a month, but the person close to the pro-Ethiopian government militia disputed this.

Reached for comment, Eritrean Information ‌Minister Yemane Gebremeskel decried "propaganda" from Ethiopia's ruling party about developments near the border but did not directly address reports about ‌military ⁠build-ups or clashes.
Spokespeople for the Ethiopian government did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

Diplomats and ⁠experts have warned of possible conflict between Ethiopia and Eritrea since fighting broke out in September between Ethiopia’s federal government and rebels in Tigray, which borders Eritrea.

Witnesses and Ethiopia's government said Eritrean forces crossed into Tigray in early October in support ​of the rebels. ACLED reported at the time ‌that drone strikes it believed were carried out by Ethiopia’s military had targeted the Eritrean troops. Ethiopia has not commented on the strikes.

Eritrea has denied any incursion into Ethiopia and accused Addis Ababa of seeking a pretext to invade its smaller neighbour, which was an Ethiopian province for three decades before gaining independence in 1993. They are now separated ‌by a border stretching more than 1,000 km (620 miles).

The fighting in Tigray has stoked fears of a ​wider conflagration in the Horn of Africa, with Ethiopia’s government also accusing Sudan, which is in the midst of its own civil war, and Egypt of backing the rebels. Eritrea, Sudan, and Egypt ⁠all deny doing so.

Ethiopia and Eritrea fought a border war from 1998 to 2000 that killed tens of thousands of people. The conflict was prompted by a dispute over the border town of Badme, which a UN boundary commission later found fell within Eritrean ‌territory.

articles.title: U.S.-Saudi nuclear agreement 'satisfactory': IAEA
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: UN nuclear watchdog head Rafael Grossi on Wednesday (November 18, 2026) welcomed a deal between the United States and Saudi Arabia on equipping the kingdom with a civilian nuclear programme.
The deal announced in July has provoked questions about the risks of nuclear proliferation.
"It's a very satisfactory outcome that we have with this agreement," Mr. Grossi told reporters after opening an International Atomic Energy Agency board of governors' meeting.
Once nuclear power development gets under way in Saudi Arabia, "we will be there," he added.

In his opening statement, Mr. Grossi told the board that the United States and Saudi Arabia in October requested the IAEA "to take the necessary steps to implement safeguards and verification measures" for their agreement.
According to the accord, the IAEA "will be provided with information about, and access to any sites for conversion, enrichment, fuel fabrication and reprocessing" in Saudi Arabia, Mr. Grossi said.
"I welcome the open, transparent approach and engagement of both governments with member states and the secretariat on this matter," he added.
Mr. Grossi told reporters the agreement was "fully aligned with the legal framework that we have at the IAEA".
He added Saudi Arabia had also agreed to "additional verification measures on a voluntary basis".
U.S. media have reported the agreement would allow Washington to export technology without the usual safeguards preventing future military use.
U.S. President Donald Trump said, just after the agreement was signed in July, that it depended on Saudi Arabia recognising Israel.

articles.title: India, Canada eye defence pact during Modi visit in December
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: India and Canada could be announcing a defence agreement during Prime Minister Narendra Modi ’s official visit in December, according to the country’s High Commissioner to Ottawa, Dinesh K. Patnaik.
Both countries are also in the final stages of negotiations of a Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement. “We are on the cusp of finalising it,” Mr. Patnaik said.

Addressing a gathering in the Canadian capital organised by the Centre for Strategic Statecraft and the Canadian International Council, he said that both countries cannot afford to let fringe issues derail their extensive mutual interests.

Mr. Patnaik took over as India’s High Commissioner to Ottawa in September 2025. Both countries had earlier expelled each other’s High Commissioners and reduced their diplomatic presence following the murder of Sikh Khalistani activist Hardeep Singh Nijjar in June 2023. Then Canadian Prime Minister Justin Trudeau accused India of orchestrating the murder, throwing bilateral relations into a tailspin. Subsequent reports by Canadian agencies also listed India, alongside China and Russia, as an interferer in domestic politics. The turnaround in ties, which began with the mutual reinstatement of High Commissioners, is set to reach a milestone with Mr. Modi’s visit on December 11 and 12.

Mr. Patnaik said India and Canada are no longer talking about a reset of their derailed relations, but rather an overarching boost in ties spanning defence, space, nuclear energy, deep tech, trade, and the mobility of people. The two nations have moved from a complete lack of trust over a year ago to an unprecedented degree of mutual trust, he added.

“The fact is that in the core strategic concerns of Canada and India, there is no conflict. Still, all it took for the entire bilateral relationship to be derailed was the fringe diaspora issue,” he said, referring to the murder of Nijjar.

“The reason was the lack of trust. India believed that Canada was actively promoting separatism in India, and Canada believed India was organising violence in Canada. We had a series of meetings between senior Ministers, NSAs of both countries, and agencies at all levels as we set about rebuilding trust. Today, we have reached the highest levels of trust, where the most sensitive areas of cooperation, such as deep tech, defence, and space, are subjects of mutual cooperation,” Mr. Patnaik said.
Cooperation between Canadian and Indian agencies remains at a high level, the High Commissioner added.

articles.title: India sitting on 'economic disaster': Rahul Gandhi at Columbia University
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi said the country’s economic model ceased to deliver results nearly a decade ago, leaving it with a deepening employment crisis and a weakened manufacturing base.

Speaking at a fireside chat at Columbia University on Tuesday (November 17, 2026), moderated by New York Times journalist Lydia Polgreen, Mr. Gandhi said India is sitting on an “economic disaster” that could become far more serious if the country continued on its present course.
“The blunt thing is that India is sitting on an economic disaster. That’s the reality of it,” he said.

“One can brush it aside, the media can brush it aside. But India has got a massive unemployment problem. India’s got a massive problem with its education system. And these are things you cannot get away from,” he added.

Mr. Gandhi identified small and medium businesses, agriculture and manufacturing as the backbone and principal engines of job creation, arguing that the services sector could not absorb India’s expanding workforce.

“The spine of the economy is small and medium business, which is the job creation engine, and agriculture. That is fundamental in India and required. The spine of the economy has been broken,” he said.

The Opposition leader said India could not achieve sustainable economic development without rebuilding its manufacturing capabilities. “We cannot survive successfully without manufacturing, it just cannot be done,” he said.
Mr. Gandhi alleged that economic growth was concentrated in a few large business groups while smaller enterprises were struggling.

“Why is there no private investment in India? Why are the only people who are growing in India, businesses that are growing in India called Adani and Ambani? Why is Tata literally being taken over by Mr. [Gautam] Adani?” he asked.

Mr. Gandhi placed the recent student-led Gen Z protests alongside resistance movements by Adivasis, Dalits and farmers against what he called the growing concentration of political and economic power in the last decade. He said the student-led protests showed that fear of “coercive power of the State” didn’t work.

“There’s a massive concentration of wealth taking place in India, and huge disenfranchisement of people. Vote is just one element of it,” he said, alleging that tribal land was being taken without consultation and that minorities, Dalits and farmers were facing growing marginalisation.

Referring to youth unemployment and economic difficulties in the U.S. and European countries, including Germany and Britain, Mr. Gandhi argued their economic challenges are serious and India’s relatively lower costs offer resilience, he said.
